newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish crown, debt firms on Moody's report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown, debt firms on Moody's report.

text.p: The Swedish crown firmed and debt yields fell on Friday after U.S. credit rating agency Moody's said the outlook for Sweden's rating had improved.
The crown managed to break a support-level at 4.45 crowns to the mark.
"The crown has firmed but the level of 4.45 crowns (to the mark) seems to be like a magnet," one dealer said.
The crown firmed to around 4.4410 to the mark from 4.4550 crowns after Moody's said the consolidation of public finances in Sweden over the past two years was positive.
Focus is on the Federal Reserve policy meeting on July 1/2.
Dealers said the market was not expecting any hike in the Fed's funds rate but one dealer said he saw two reasons for yields to rise in the near future.
"I think yields can come up partly because people are a bit cautious ahead of the FOMC-meeting and partly because of some half year-effects," he said.
Six month T-bill rate fell one basis point to 4.14 percent and the ten year bond yield fell two basis points to 6.65 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.4460 crowns to the mark versus 4.4595 crowns late Thursday. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1071
